annotations.text:
TODAY
One Model tab carries credentials and tier bindings
together.
The binding row needs ~730px and has 552px, so max
tokens and temperature wrap into two number boxes
with no visible label — on every screen size, not just
small ones.

MODEL TAB — TIERS ONLY
Credentials moved out, so the tab holds three cards and
nothing else, and the modal only needs 896px.
No provider select: the binding is model-first, so you can
no longer pick a provider without a model — which is the
bug at model-tab.tsx:96 that PUTs model_id: "".

The Fast tier shows the state the split makes likelier: a
tier bound to a provider you have not connected.
put_config validates only that the model exists in the
catalog, never that its provider is configured, and
ModelResolver's degradation path covers agent overrides
only — a tier binding raises ModelConfigError instead.
So this warning is load-bearing, not decorative.

MODEL PICKER
At 15 providers nobody thinks "I want an OpenRouter
model" — they think "I want Kimi K2" or "the cheapest
thing with 1M context".
So one search across every connected provider, with the
deciding facts on the row: context window, price per Mtok,
thinking style.
Suggested-for-this-tier comes from suggested_tier, which
the catalog already carries.
Unconnected providers stay reachable from the footer
rather than being filtered out of existence.

PROVIDERS TAB — NEW
Search, an All / Connected / Available filter, and grouping
by status — the things a 15-row list needs and a 4-row
section never did.
The subtitle draws the line that matters: these grant no
access to your accounts, unlike /integrations.

Note the auth-type chips. Bedrock wants region + SigV4,
Azure wants endpoint + deployment + api-version. At this
scale the credential form is per-provider, not a fixed
(api_key, base_url) pair — extra_config on CredentialBody
is the hook that already exists.

AT PHONE WIDTH
The modal becomes a full sheet and the tab rail becomes a
list you push from — no horizontal tab scroller, no fixed
600px box.
The 4-column grid folds to 2 with Model spanning both.
Controls go to 44px. The Save bar stays pinned.

EXPLORED EARLIER — kept for the record, not proposed
Both of these assumed Providers and Tiers share one surface. Splitting them made the question moot:
the Model tab no longer needs a full page (B), and the drill-in navigation (C) moved into the Providers
list where a long list actually wants it.
